newsitem.title: USA: US junk corp bond deals roll ahead on strong techs.
newsitem.headline: US junk corp bond deals roll ahead on strong techs.

text.p: Strong technicals in the junk bond market continue to foster a positive environment for new junk bond deals, which are expected to dominate Friday's U.S. corporate bond new issue calendar, syndicate officials said. The junk bond market received yet another week of healthy inflows of new cash from mutual funds late Thursday. AMG Data Services reported junk bond funds received net cash inflows of $296 million in the latest week.
"I think this is what people were expecting," said one official. "Everything is going in the right direction, and there is no reason to expect (new issuance) will slow down."
After being dominated by emerging market deals this week, Friday's calendar is expected to consist primarily of domestic junk bond issuers.

Standard Commercial Tobacco Co Inc is preparing to sell $100 million in senior notes due 2005 via BT Securities Corp. Price talk on the deal, which is rated B1/BB-minus, is around nine percent, sources said.
Standard Commercial, based in Wilson, N.C., is the third largest tobacco processor in U.S. The company is contracted by major cigarette makers to shred tobacco leaf for use in their products.
A source close to the deal said the company is not involved in the current tobacco settlement or any other tobacco-related litigation.
Even if the settlement is approved, the company expects to reap the benefits of growth of tobacco usage internationally, the source said.

Elsewhere, Western Financial Bank is expected to sell $150 million in subordinated debentures due 2007 via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. Price talk on the deal, rated B1/B-plus, is around the 250 basis point-spread level.

Digital TV Services is also expected to sell $155 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via DLJ later on Friday. The deal, rated B3/CCC, includes a two-year prefunded interest reserve. Price talk is in the 12 percent area, sources said.
Digital TV, a privately-held company based in Roswell, Ga., is an exclusive distributor of direct broadcast satellite system, DIRECTV, with around 88,000 subscribers.
Earlier on Friday, GCI Inc, a unit of GCI General Communications Inc, sold $180 million in 10-year senior notes (B2/B-plus) to yield 9.75 percent via Salomon Brothers Inc.
The deal was increased from an original size of $150 million.
General Communication is a diversified telecommunications company, providing long-distance telephone and cable services in Alaska.
